proposals.approach:
Fewest moving parts, verified against live code: two new leaf interfaces slotted into the exact extend-point Presence already proved (IPlatformServices growth, private-ctor-plus-static-Create per OS), one new member on the existing IPlatformFileSystem instead of a third new interface, and one new OS-uniform adapter reused by all three OSes instead of three separate ones. Every ledger "new" capability (ground-output.json verdicts: daemon-process-lifetime, login-startup-registration, on-demand-service-start, single-instance-lock, lock-liveness-probe — all "new", both lenses empty) lands on an existing owner wherever one already fits, and only two genuinely new interfaces get built.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS (verified live, not assumed): IPlatformServices today has exactly two members, FileSystem and Presence (src/AgentGuard.Abstractions/Contracts/IPlatformServices.cs:11-23), each grown the identical way — an interface in Abstractions.Contracts, one implementer per OS with a private constructor and a static Create(), wired inside each per-OS PlatformServices.Create() (src/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.MacOS/Posix/PlatformServices.cs:20-53, .../PlatformServices.MacOS.cs, .../PlatformServices.Linux.cs, src/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Windows/Windows/PlatformServices.cs:19-50). Where mac and Linux share a mechanism byte-for-byte, the file itself is link-shared (AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Linux.csproj compiles PlatformServices.cs/PosixFileSystem.cs/PosixNativeMethods.cs straight out of the MacOS project); where they diverge, the shared file declares a private static partial method and each OS supplies its own body in its own fragment file (PlatformServices.CreatePresence(), PosixFileSystem.TryQueryNativeCaseSensitivity). doctor/install already share one detect-and-repair extend point, ISetupCondition (Detect returns ConditionState.Ok/Broken(reason)/CannotVerify(reason); Repair returns RepairOutcome.Repaired/NoChangeNeeded/NotRepairable(reason)) collected into three static lists in SetupConditions.cs that install and doctor both iterate with zero new Program.cs wiring (src/AgentGuard.Engine/Setup/ISetupCondition.cs, SetupConditions.cs, SetupCommands.cs:146-180). AG0011's owner table (analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers/OwnedPrimitives.cs) already bans System.Diagnostics.Process/ProcessStartInfo and System.IO.FileStream everywhere with no owner (confirmed live: zero production call sites of either, plus a passing proving test for each); I confirmed by direct grep that System.Threading.Mutex is not in this table at all today — a raw `new Mutex(...)` anywhere in the tree currently compiles clean, ungoverned.

THE TWO NEW INTERFACES (Abstractions.Contracts, both reached as new IPlatformServices properties — this is the public-interface change needing Tim's sign-off):

`ISingleInstanceLock { IDisposable? TryAcquire(); }` — one method that serves BOTH ledger capabilities (single-instance-lock and lock-liveness-probe) that Tim's own recorded design already treats as the same object used two ways: appd calls TryAcquire once and holds the handle for its process lifetime (releasing it on exit is the OS's job — the recorded spike already proved SIGKILL leaves no stale lock on either mechanism, so no extra shutdown-signal plumbing is needed); the CLI probe calls TryAcquire, and if it gets a handle back, immediately disposes it (nobody was holding it — not running) instead of holding it, then triggers the canonical start. Building this as two separate methods, or two separate interfaces, would be an unjustified second path for what is one primitive used two ways (SOLID rail 4). Implementers: a POSIX class (mac-authored, linux-linked, same convention as PosixFileSystem) opening a FileStream at a fixed path with FileShare.None, with one small per-OS partial fragment for which env var supplies the runtime-dir root (TMPDIR on macOS — the already-approved AGS5443 exemption applies at exactly this call site; XDG_RUNTIME_DIR on Linux — no exemption needed there, confirmed live that this variable is read nowhere in the tree today); and a Windows class wrapping a `Local\`-scoped named Mutex. Before opening the lock file, the POSIX implementer needs the `agentguard/` subdirectory created at mode 0700 (conversation.md's own decided fact) — raw `Directory.CreateDirectory`+`SetUnixFileMode` there would itself be reported by the existing AG0101 rule (confirmed live: that rule already bans exactly these OS-divergent static members outside the one class implementing IPlatformFileSystem), so rather than opening a THIRD new interface for this, the simplest correct move is one new member on the interface that already owns exactly this class of concern — `IPlatformFileSystem.EnsurePrivateDirectory(string path)` (POSIX bodies do it for real; the Windows implementer throws, mirroring the existing MakeExecutable-on-Windows-throws precedent). Because IPlatformFileSystem is already a protected, wired-in leaf, this addition needs zero analyzer changes to be enforced — it inherits AG0025/AG0030/AG0101's existing protection for free. This is itself a second, smaller public-interface change alongside the IPlatformServices one and should be surfaced to Tim as such, not folded silently into the first.

`IDaemonStartup { DaemonRegistrationResult DetectRegistration(string expectedBinaryPath); void Register(string binaryPath); void StartNow(); }`, with `DaemonRegistrationResult(DaemonRegistrationStatus Status, string Detail)` in Contracts and `DaemonRegistrationStatus { Registered, Missing, WrongBinary, CannotVerify }` in the Abstractions root namespace — this mirrors PresenceResult/ApprovalReason's exact placement and shape (a per-OS boundary returns a plain reason plus a human-readable detail; the OS-agnostic Engine layer maps that into whatever it needs). `expectedBinaryPath`/`binaryPath` must be the STABLE launcher (MachinePaths.BinGuard(context), the same `~/.agentguard/bin/guard` every hook and PATH entry already points at — src/AgentGuard.Engine/Setup/MachinePaths.cs:130-140), never SetupContext.ResolvedBinaryPath (the specific-version path of whatever binary happens to be running) — passing the wrong one would silently break autostart on the very next version upgrade, since the registration would still point at a version directory `install` may since have pruned or replaced. Implementers follow the identical mac-shared/linux-linked/windows-separate shape as Presence: macOS writes/reads the `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.4thwaiv.agentguard.appd.plist` file and shells out to `launchctl kickstart`; Linux writes/reads `~/.config/systemd/user/agentguard-appd.service` and shells out to `systemctl --user start`; Windows shells out to `schtasks` for both registration and on-demand start, all naming decisions already settled in conversation.md. Each of these three literal identifiers is used by exactly one class (unlike PolkitAction.Id, which has two consumers — the C# check and a shipped policy file — and is why THAT one has a shared owner); per DRY rail 5, each identifier is simply an internal const inside its own single per-OS class, with no shared cross-OS constants file, since nothing else references it.

THE ONE NEW OS-UNIFORM ADAPTER: every per-OS IDaemonStartup implementer needs to run an external command and read its exit code (and, on Windows, its stdout, to answer DetectRegistration from `schtasks /Query`) — but the ACT of launching a process and waiting for it is mechanically identical on all three OSes; only the command line differs, which is data the per-OS classes already own. Rather than growing three separate per-OS owners for Process/ProcessStartInfo (which would need AG0011 gated to `IsAnyPerOsImplementationLibrary`), the simpler and more correct placement — verified against the existing convention where RandomGeneratorAdapter (also OS-uniform) lives in core AgentGuard.CrossPlatform and is handed out through the single CrossPlatformAdapters.Create() bundle (src/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform/CrossPlatformAdapters.cs, RandomGeneratorAdapter.cs) — is one new `IProcessLauncher` interface with one implementer, `ProcessLauncherAdapter`, in core AgentGuard.CrossPlatform, added as a new property on CrossPlatformAdapters and pulled by each per-OS PlatformServices.Create() the same way it already pulls PlatformFileSystemComposition.Create(). This is a direct application of best-practices 2d (dependencies point one way, service placed at its lowest actual consumer) and means System.Diagnostics.Process/ProcessStartInfo need exactly ONE new AG0011 owner entry, not three — the per-OS Startup classes never touch Process directly at all.

DAEMON PROCESS LIFETIME needs no new interface at all: the `daemon` verb's handler calls `services.Platform.DaemonLock.TryAcquire()`; null means refuse with a clear message and exit non-zero (fail closed, best-practices 5a/5b); non-null means hold the handle and block indefinitely (a plain `Task.Delay(Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan, ct)` or equivalent) until the process is killed, at which point the OS itself releases the lock — proven safe by the recorded spike, so no signal-handling plumbing is a decision item here. Per Tim's recorded decision, `daemon` does not call ApprovalGate — and nothing needs to newly forbid a workaround here, because AG0108 already confines every call to IPresenceCheck.Check to ApprovalGate itself, so a "half-gate" bypass is already impossible.

WIRING INTO THE EXISTING SURFACE, reusing rather than inventing: (1) a new `DaemonRegistrationCondition : ISetupCondition` added to both SetupConditions.Machine (doctor detects it) and SetupConditions.MachineStructural (install establishes it) — Detect calls IDaemonStartup.DetectRegistration and maps DaemonRegistrationStatus to ConditionState exactly the way MacOsPresenceCheck already maps a native result to ApprovalReason through a small pure Map function; Repair calls IDaemonStartup.Register. This gives doctor's existing report-and---fix-repair behavior for free, with no new CLI plumbing (src/AgentGuard.Engine/Setup/SetupCommands.cs:146-180 already iterates whichever list applies). (2) One new Engine-level static helper, `DaemonAvailability.EnsureRunning(ISystemServices services)`, the single reusable "probe the lock, and if nobody holds it, call StartNow" entry point Tim's own words call for ("any that needs to deal with the appd... multiple will need to call it inside of their service code") — giving that dance one owner instead of letting each future caller reinvent it (SOLID rail 1). (3) Two new CLI verbs added to Program.cs's fixed BuildRootCommand list (src/AgentGuard.Cli/Program.cs:65-75) alongside the existing six: `daemon` (ungated, the process-lifetime body above) and `status` (reports whether appd is running, per Tim's decision).

OPEN QUESTION I AM NOT SILENTLY RESOLVING: whether `status` itself calls DaemonAvailability.EnsureRunning (a side-effecting "check and fix" command) or stays a pure read-only probe-and-report like doctor-without---fix. Tim's words support both readings equally well ("status... is the first consumer of the running check" names the check, not necessarily the start), and it changes status's public contract (best-practices 4b: a command's behavior is exactly the kind of thing that locks in once shipped). Without an explicit pick, issue #63's own "Done when" line — "the CLI starts it through the same canonical path when it is not running" — has no CLI-visible proof anywhere in this design's owned verb surface (install only registers; daemon is the thing being started, not the trigger); I flag this rather than quietly deciding it either way.
keySteps: Add ISingleInstanceLock (TryAcquire(): IDisposable?) to AgentGuard.Abstractions.Contracts; implement once in a POSIX class (FileStream+FileShare.None, mac-authored/linux-linked, one partial fragment for TMPDIR vs XDG_RUNTIME_DIR) and once in a Windows class (Local\-scoped named Mutex).

Add DaemonRegistrationStatus enum (AgentGuard.Abstractions) and DaemonRegistrationResult record + IDaemonStartup interface (DetectRegistration/Register/StartNow) to Contracts; implement once per OS (mac/linux share the file via partial methods for each op, since launchctl/systemctl differ completely; Windows is a separate class using schtasks for all three).

Grow IPlatformFileSystem with EnsurePrivateDirectory(string path) (POSIX: mkdir+chmod 0700 via the OS-divergent statics already legal only inside this owner; Windows: throws) so the lock's directory permission need reuses an already-governed owner instead of opening a third interface.

Add IProcessLauncher (Abstractions.Contracts) + ProcessLauncherAdapter, the single OS-uniform owner of System.Diagnostics.Process/ProcessStartInfo, in core AgentGuard.CrossPlatform; expose it as a new property on CrossPlatformAdapters the same way RandomGeneratorAdapter already is, and inject it into each per-OS IDaemonStartup implementer — none of them touch Process directly.

Add DaemonLock and DaemonStartup properties to IPlatformServices; wire both into every per-OS PlatformServices.Create() (mac/linux/windows), the same door Presence already uses — this is the public-interface change that needs Tim's explicit sign-off before ARCHITECTURE freezes it.

Add DaemonRegistrationCondition (ISetupCondition) to SetupConditions.Machine and .MachineStructural, mapping DaemonRegistrationStatus to ConditionState/RepairOutcome via a small pure Map function, the same shape MacOsPresenceCheck already uses for its native result.

Add AgentGuard.Setup.DaemonAvailability.EnsureRunning(ISystemServices) as the one shared probe-then-StartNow helper; every present and future command that needs appd running calls this one owner rather than re-deriving the dance.

Add the `daemon` verb to Program.cs (ungated per Tim's decision; TryAcquire, hold-or-refuse, block indefinitely on success) and the `status` verb (reports whether appd is running) to BuildRootCommand's existing six-verb list.

Carry the AGS5443 macOS-lock-path suppression and the two OwnedPrimitives.cs table additions into the contract's Decisions section verbatim, per conversation.md's own explicit must-carry requirement — both are top-severity Lie-catcher findings if the contract does not carry them across.

Get Tim's explicit answer on whether `status` triggers EnsureRunning (side-effecting) or stays probe-and-report only (read-only), before TDD writes its acceptance test — this is the one open fork this design surfaces rather than silently picking.

rulesToAdd.failureModeStopped: Without a deliberate, reviewed owner entry, the first implementer who needs to shell out to launchctl/systemctl/schtasks hits a hard build error with only two visible ways out: reach for a raw allow-list/suppression at whatever call site they're standing in (an unapproved exception to a settled rule per rails-decisions), or scatter three separate ad hoc Process-owning classes across the per-OS assemblies instead of the one shared owner — reopening exactly the kind of duplicated primitive-handling DRY exists to prevent.
rulesToAdd.analyzer: Table entry in the existing RawPrimitiveOnlyInOwnerAnalyzer (AG0011) — no new analyzer class, one new OwnedPrimitives.cs entry plus a compliant/violating proving test pair, the same mechanism already used for every other primitive in that table.

rulesToAdd.rule: Extend the same AG0011 table so System.IO.FileStream resolves to OwnedBy(the ISingleInstanceLock POSIX implementer's identity, CrossPlatformBoundary.IsAnyPerOsImplementationLibrary) instead of BannedEverywhere.
rulesToAdd.failureModeStopped: Without this, an implementer who needs the exclusive-lock FileStream call either gets stuck at a build error with the same escape-hatch temptation as above, or (worse) opens the FileStream inside some other convenient class in the same assembly instead of the one dedicated lock owner, silently un-concentrating the single-instance invariant SOLID rail 1 requires stay in one place.
rulesToAdd.analyzer: Table entry in the existing RawPrimitiveOnlyInOwnerAnalyzer (AG0011), reusing the exact gate function (CrossPlatformBoundary.IsAnyPerOsImplementationLibrary) AG0101 already defines for the filesystem owner — no new gate to invent.

rulesToAdd.rule: Add a NEW AG0011 table entry for System.Threading.Mutex (there is no entry for it today at all — confirmed by direct grep of OwnedPrimitives.cs, RawPrimitiveOnlyInOwnerAnalyzer.cs, and MemberUseScanner.cs) resolving to OwnedBy(the ISingleInstanceLock Windows implementer's identity, CrossPlatformBoundary.IsAnyPerOsImplementationLibrary).
rulesToAdd.failureModeStopped: Today, `new Mutex(...)` compiles clean anywhere in the entire codebase, including AgentGuard.Engine (which is supposed to stay OS-agnostic and touch no OS synchronization primitive directly) or any other assembly not otherwise gated — this work is the first to need a named Mutex at all, and shipping it without closing this gap leaves a real, previously-unnoticed hole in the analyzer fence for the very primitive this same issue introduces, discoverable by nothing already in the repo.
rulesToAdd.analyzer: Same mechanism as the two entries above — a third OwnedPrimitives.cs table row, no new analyzer class. conversation.md itself flags this exact question as open for RULE-PHASE; this is the recommendation to close it rather than leave it open.

rulesToAdd.rule: A new check verifying that every public interface in AgentGuard.Abstractions.Contracts with a real (non-test) implementing class is reachable from ISystemServices's own container walk (i.e., present in BoundaryServices's derived-services set) — flagging one that is not.
rulesToAdd.failureModeStopped: AG0025/AG0030 only protect an interface they can SEE via that walk (confirmed live: OneOwnerPerInterfaceAnalyzer.cs derives its candidate set entirely from BoundaryServices.Resolve() starting at ISystemServices). An interface built correctly today — say ISingleInstanceLock or IDaemonStartup — but never wired onto IPlatformServices (a copy-paste miss, or a rebase that drops the two-line property addition while keeping the implementer classes) would have exactly one implementer today and ZERO protection against a second one appearing later, with nothing in the existing rule set able to notice. This work is adding two brand-new Contracts interfaces in one pass, which is exactly the moment this blind spot is most likely to bite.
rulesToAdd.analyzer: A new DiagnosticAnalyzer sitting beside OneOwnerPerInterfaceAnalyzer (AG0025), consuming the same BoundaryServices walk in the opposite direction (implementer-with-no-reachable-owner rather than owner-with-two-implementers).

rulesToAdd.rule: (Lower confidence — flagged for RULE-PHASE to assess feasibility, not a firm recommendation) An argument-shape check on every call to IDaemonStartup.Register/DetectRegistration requiring the binary-path argument to be MachinePaths.BinGuard(...) (or a value reached through it), never SetupContext.ResolvedBinaryPath directly.
rulesToAdd.failureModeStopped: Passing the resolved-running-binary path instead of the stable launcher path compiles fine (both are plain strings) and looks correct in a quick manual test, but silently breaks autostart on the very next version upgrade once the version-pinned path install pointed at is pruned or replaced — a quiet, delayed failure with no compiler signal, exactly the kind of easy, unnoticed corner-cut this issue's own 'a registration pointing at the wrong binary' failure mode describes.
rulesToAdd.analyzer: Would need to match on the argument EXPRESSION shape rather than a type identity, unlike every rule above — closer to AG0109's 'read through the one sanctioned accessor' pattern than to AG0011's type-keyed table, and correspondingly more work to build correctly; worth a feasibility look but not as certain a win as the three table entries above.

risks: The exact per-OS body of Register() on macOS/Linux is not yet empirically verified: writing the plist/unit file may not be sufficient by itself for an immediate StartNow() (launchctl kickstart / systemctl --user start) to succeed in the same already-running login session — launchd/systemd may need an explicit 'notice this new/changed unit now' step (launchctl bootstrap, systemctl --user daemon-reload) before kickstart/start can find it. The recorded spike proved lock semantics (FileStream/Mutex behavior across sessions, stale-lock behavior on SIGKILL) but did not exercise the full register-then-start round trip. If true, Register() needs the shared IProcessLauncher on macOS/Linux too, not just Windows — this does not change the interface shape proposed here, but it does change what each per-OS Register() body must do, and should be nailed down empirically before IMPLEMENT, not assumed.

Whether `status` triggers DaemonAvailability.EnsureRunning (side-effecting) or stays a pure probe-and-report (read-only) is a genuine, unresolved fork in a public CLI command's contract (best-practices 4b territory) — addressed as an explicit open question above, not silently picked, because it also determines whether issue #63 ships any CLI-visible proof of its own 'the CLI starts it through the same canonical path when it is not running' acceptance line.

This proposal's exact interface member split (two flat IPlatformServices siblings, DaemonLock and DaemonStartup, plus one new IPlatformFileSystem member) is one defensible shape among others (for example, nesting both under one IPlatformServices.Daemon container interface, mirroring how IFileSystem nests its four leaves) — Tim's own recorded note that the ground explorers 'tried to lock in a design too early' on this exact question applies equally to this proposal; it should be presented as a recommendation to sign off, not treated as already settled.

The AGS5443 suppression for the macOS lock path, and the AG0011 table additions for Process/FileStream (already Tim-approved in conversation.md) plus the new Mutex entry this proposal adds, all live inside analyzers/ and must be carried into the contract's Decisions section verbatim — conversation.md itself names this as a run-failing omission if missed, not a minor documentation gap.

Pointed-integration test coverage for the two new per-OS mechanisms (the POSIX FileStream lock and the Windows Mutex, plus each OS's real launchctl/systemctl/schtasks round trip) needs the same per-OS-real-adapter treatment the presence work already established (best-practices 6a) — a unit test against a fake cannot prove the cross-session lock behavior the spike already demonstrated matters; this is TDD's stage to detail, but the need should not be lost between DESIGN and TDD.

autoResolved.choice: Whether the single-instance lock (an acquire/release synchronization primitive) needs a full owned interface-plus-factory, or can stay a lighter-weight passed-around value.
autoResolved.resolution: Give it a full owned interface (ISingleInstanceLock) with a private-constructor-and-static-Create implementer per OS — the same shape every other stateful boundary type in this codebase already uses.
autoResolved.principle: 2e — Escalate a boundary abstraction the moment the lightweight version gets complex.
autoResolved.evidence: A single-instance lock is exactly the 'stateful object you can act on the world through' 2e describes (you acquire and release through it, it is not inert data), so it gets the full owned-interface-plus-factory treatment 2e mandates — the same treatment FileInfo/DirectoryInfo already received behind IFileInfo/IDirectoryInfo (src/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform/AbstractedFileInfo.cs) for the identical reason.

autoResolved.choice: Where the new OS-uniform process-launching owner (needed by every per-OS canonical-start implementer) should live.
autoResolved.resolution: In AgentGuard.CrossPlatform — the lowest assembly that actually consumes it (all three per-OS assemblies, through CrossPlatformAdapters) — never injected up from AgentGuard.Boundaries or AgentGuard.Engine.
autoResolved.principle: 2d — Dependencies point one way.
autoResolved.evidence: Matches the guide's own worked example verbatim ('the GUID service lives in AgentGuard.CrossPlatform, not injected up from AgentGuard.Boundaries, which depends on it'); RandomGeneratorAdapter — confirmed live at src/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform/RandomGeneratorAdapter.cs — already lives in exactly this assembly for the identical reason, and the new process-launcher owner follows the same placement rule.

autoResolved.choice: Whether the new daemon capabilities (login-startup registration, on-demand start, the single-instance lock) may branch on the current OS inline inside OS-agnostic code, or must be isolated behind an owned per-OS interface.
autoResolved.resolution: Isolated behind two new owned interfaces (ISingleInstanceLock, IDaemonStartup) in AgentGuard.Abstractions.Contracts, each with one implementation per OS — no inline OS branching anywhere else.
autoResolved.principle: 1b — OS-agnostic by default; OS-difference is the rare exception, isolated behind the platform interface.
autoResolved.evidence: Confirmed live that AG0009 already forbids any OperatingSystem.Is*/RuntimeInformation.IsOSPlatform call outside the four AgentGuard.CrossPlatform* assemblies (analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers/NoOsBranchingOutsideCrossPlatformAnalyzer.cs), so the only compliant shape for code reached from AgentGuard.Engine/AgentGuard.Cli is an owned interface with per-OS implementations — exactly the shape IPresenceCheck and IPlatformFileSystem already use.

autoResolved.choice: What text encoding the new login-startup registration files (the plist / systemd unit content) are written with.
autoResolved.resolution: UTF-8 without a byte-order mark — no new encoding decision or parameter is needed.
autoResolved.principle: 4a — Text is UTF-8 without a byte-order mark, unless an existing file or a required format says otherwise.
autoResolved.evidence: The write reuses the existing IFileWriter.WriteAllText(path, contents); its only production implementation, FileWriterAdapter (src/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform/FileWriterAdapter.cs:30), calls File.WriteAllText with no explicit Encoding argument, which .NET defaults to UTF-8 without a BOM — already a verified live fact (ground-output.json, install-and-setup area, fact 15). The new registration write adds no new writer, so it inherits this for free.

autoResolved.choice: Whether the new per-OS lock/startup classes may be constructed ad hoc by whatever code needs them, or must arrive through the existing container-and-factory composition.
autoResolved.resolution: Built exactly once inside each per-OS PlatformServices.Create(), constructor-injected into the container the same way Presence and the file system already are; no caller ever news one up.
autoResolved.principle: 6a — Every dependency is injected through an interface so a test can substitute it; a class never news-up its own dependency.
autoResolved.evidence: Mirrors the locked, already-verified shape every existing IPlatformServices member uses: private constructor, one static Create(), wired through the single PlatformServices.Create() door (src/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.MacOS/Posix/PlatformServices.cs:20-53; src/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Windows/Windows/PlatformServices.cs:19-50).

autoResolved.choice: Whether the daemon verb's process-lifetime loop needs its own signal-handling or graceful-shutdown mechanism to avoid leaving a stale lock behind on a crash.
autoResolved.resolution: No — the OS itself already provides this for free (both lock mechanisms release immediately on process death), so no new shutdown-handling code is a decision item here.
autoResolved.principle: 5a — Fail closed is the default; assert every expectation, and when one does not hold, fail closed.
autoResolved.evidence: conversation.md's recorded spike: 'After the holder was killed with SIGKILL, both the named mutex and the file lock were immediately available again, so a killed daemon cannot block its own restart' — the OS's own release-on-death behavior already satisfies fail-closed here, so adding a bespoke shutdown-signal seam would be unneeded new surface rather than a requirement.

proposals.approach:
Scope check against the live issue first: #63 is process-only (start, singleton, findable, login-registered) — no key, dashboard, identity check, or channel. Everything below builds exactly that, generally, with zero speculative reach into #64-#67.

THE CORE DESIGN — three new owned capabilities, placed by the SAME rules that already govern every capability in this tree:

1. ISingleInstanceLock (new interface, AgentGuard.Abstractions.Contracts) — one operation, TryAcquire, used identically by the daemon (which keeps the returned handle for its life) and by the CLI/doctor probe (which disposes it immediately if acquired). Tim's own reasoning for the lock-as-running-check ("nothing extra to build and nothing that can disagree with it") is itself the argument against a second, separate IsHeld-style method: one seam, two calling patterns, never two mechanisms that could disagree. Two implementers, matching the two real primitives the spike proved: WindowsSingleInstanceLock (CrossPlatform.Windows, a Local\ named Mutex — Local\ is what gives Windows its logon-session scope for free) and a shared PosixSingleInstanceLock (an exclusive FileStream at FileShare.None), link-shared macOS→Linux exactly the way PlatformServices.cs/PosixFileSystem.cs/PosixNativeMethods.cs already are, with a private-partial fragment per OS supplying only the one thing that differs — which env var roots the lock directory ($TMPDIR vs $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR) — the identical shape CreatePresence() already uses to vary the presence check per POSIX OS.

2. IServiceRegistration (new interface) — IsRegistered / Register / TriggerStart on ONE interface, not three, because they are three operations on one OS object (the registered login-time service entry), and issue #63 itself ties them together: "the CLI's check-and-start is the fallback... not a replacement for [login registration]" — register and start are the same launchctl/systemctl/schtasks surface, just different subcommands. Three implementers (MacOsServiceRegistration, LinuxServiceRegistration, WindowsServiceRegistration) — not link-shared, because the underlying OS objects are genuinely distinct (a plist file vs. a unit file vs. a Task Scheduler object, the last of which is "not a filesystem path" at all per ground's own surface list).

3. IProcessLauncher (new interface) — a thin, faithful mirror of Process.Start/WaitForExit/ExitCode (per 2c: mirror the primitive, not policy), ONE OS-uniform implementer (ProcessLauncherAdapter) owned in the core AgentGuard.CrossPlatform assembly — the same home as RandomGeneratorAdapter/CrossPlatformAdapters, for the same reason: it is consumed by the per-OS registration classes one layer up, and core CrossPlatform is the lowest of the three layers (Boundaries -> per-OS -> core CrossPlatform, confirmed live: CrossPlatformAdapters.Create() and RandomGeneratorAdapter.Create() are both called directly, never injected, by every per-OS PlatformServices.Create()). This is the FULL general seam for "run an external command" — the first one this codebase has ever needed (polkit deliberately avoided this via D-Bus) — used by all three registration classes for detection (launchctl print / systemctl --user status / schtasks /Query), for the on-demand start, and for Windows's schtasks-based registration itself, rather than three hand-rolled, near-duplicate Process.Start fragments each carrying their own ad hoc AG0011 exception.

THE LAYERING INSIGHT THIS DESIGN TURNS ON: PlatformServices.Create() is parameter-less today and must stay that way — handing it a Boundaries-built value (e.g. an IEnvironment built inside SystemServices.Create()) would be exactly the forbidden shape SOLID rail 8 names ("Boundaries passing a service into CrossPlatform, which Boundaries references"), because SystemServices.Create() builds `platform` BEFORE it builds `environment`. Two different, already-precedented answers apply depending on what the new code actually needs: (a) IProcessLauncher is owned in core CrossPlatform, one layer BELOW the per-OS registration classes, so it is reached by direct construction at Create()-time exactly like PosixFileSystem.Create(parts.Shared, parts.Factory) already is — no injection-direction problem exists because nothing crosses from Boundaries. (b) The registration classes' genuinely Boundaries-owned inputs (home directory, the resolved binary path, IFileReader/IFileWriter) are NOT threaded into Create() at all — they are already fully known, already-resolved VALUES that SetupContext computes today (context.HomeDirectory, context.ResolvedBinaryPath, context.FileReader/FileWriter) and simply gets one more field to carry (ServiceRegistration), following the exact precedent of its existing `FileSystem = services.Platform.FileSystem` field. IServiceRegistration's methods then take these as plain, explicit, already-resolved parameters — not the whole ISystemServices — because unlike presence (whose per-OS boundary needs are genuinely unpredictable, which is why IPresenceCheck.Check takes the full container) this capability's input set is small and fully known ahead of time. Where a value genuinely can't be pre-resolved by a SetupContext-holding caller (DaemonAvailability and the daemon verb itself are NOT SetupCommands-family code and hold ISystemServices directly), the caller resolves it itself (services.Environment.GetTempDirectory()/GetEnvironmentVariable) and passes the resulting string into TryAcquire — Windows's implementer simply ignores it, the same OS-asymmetric-parameter shape IPlatformFileSystem.IsExecutable(path)/IsCaseSensitive(path) already use.

ENGINE + CLI ORCHESTRATION: a new AgentGuard.Setup.DaemonAvailability is the single owner of the "is appd running" / "make sure appd is running" invariant — IsRunning(services) (probe via TryAcquire-then-release) and EnsureRunningAsync(services) (probe, then ServiceRegistration.TriggerStart when not running). This directly answers Tim's own "no fixed list... multiple will need to call it inside their service code" — the seam is reusable by design, and for #63 itself it has exactly one required caller: SetupCommands.Install, after its existing condition loop succeeds, so "installing onto an already-running login session" (the case the issue calls out by name) is actually satisfied rather than left to the next login. A new ServiceRegistrationCondition implements ISetupCondition directly (not MachineCondition — it has no dependency on InstallState/MachineFacts, unlike the four existing machine conditions), added to SetupConditions.MachineStructural after BinSymlinkCondition so it can point the registration at the now-established bin/guard launcher; doctor's existing detect/repair loop reports and repairs it with zero new CLI wiring, exactly the extend-point ground already found proven. A new AgentGuard.Setup.DaemonCommand.Run(services, ct) is the daemon verb's body: TryAcquire and hold (a clean, actionable non-zero exit if already held, per Tim's "clear about what went wrong and how to fix" decision — never a crash), then block on Task.Delay(Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan, ct) until the OS/service manager kills it. No cooperative shutdown mechanism is proposed: issue #63's Done-when criteria require only that appd "stays up" and "survives the CLI exiting," and the spike already proved both lock primitives self-clear on SIGKILL/TerminateProcess — building a shutdown-signal abstraction now, with no stated need, would itself be the premature escape hatch rail 7 forbids. The CLI gains exactly two verbs — `daemon` (ungated, joining the doctor/hook/version group per Tim's "lazy verify" decision) and `status` (reports DaemonAvailability.IsRunning) — each an ordinary BuildXCommand(services) factory added to BuildRootCommand; AG0017's existing composition-point pin (matched by assembly identity, not an enumerated verb list) already covers both with no analyzer changes.

WHY THIS IS THE GENERAL SEAM, NOT A HACK: the rejected alternative is inlining Process.Start("launchctl", "kickstart ...") directly at each of the 2-3 call sites that need it, one bespoke [SuppressMessage] per site — that duplicates the shell-out three times with no shared owner (a DRY rail-6 violation) and never gets a fake, so nothing above it is unit-testable (rail 6a). The rejected shortcut on registration is checking only "does the plist file exist" — cheaper, but wrong on Windows (no file exists at all) and incomplete on POSIX (a written-but-never-loaded unit file false-positives as registered while never firing at login) — exactly the easy-half shortcut rail 1 forbids, silently dropping the case the issue's Done-when criteria is actually about. Building the three interfaces above, correctly placed on the first pass, is what "no deferred abstraction" requires.

WHAT THIS PROPOSES vs. WHAT IS DECIDED: the mechanisms (mutex vs. file lock, launchctl/systemctl/schtasks, the naming convention) are Tim's own recorded decisions in conversation.md and are treated here as fixed ground truth. The THREE NEW PUBLIC INTERFACES, their placement, and their exact members are this architect's proposal for the open question ground flagged ("DESIGN's to propose and Tim's to sign off") — not yet approved, and must be surfaced to Tim before ARCHITECTURE begins.

proposals.approach:
Make the wrong daemon inexpressible at the type level, then fence what is left with rules copied from mechanisms this repo already ships.

**The three ways this work goes wrong, and what each costs the human.** (1) The AI produces a second start path — spawning `~/.agentguard/bin/guard daemon` directly instead of asking the service manager — because `Process` is right there once it has an owner. Cost: a daemon that dies with the terminal, and the divergent startup mechanism issue #63 exists to forbid. (2) The AI fakes the single-instance check — a pid file, `IFileReader.Exists`, or `launchctl print` — because `FileStream`/`Mutex` are banned and growing an owner is work. Cost: two daemons, which is the one thing the "Done when" names. (3) The AI reaches `$TMPDIR` through `IEnvironment.GetEnvironmentVariable("TMPDIR")` so `AGS5443` never fires. `conversation.md` names this exact dodge and forbids it, and **nothing in the tree catches it today** — `GetEnvironmentVariable` is a generic pass-through (`src/AgentGuard.Boundaries/EnvironmentAdapter.cs:19-33`). Every structural choice below is picked because it kills one of these.

**Shape.** One new sub-container `IPlatformDaemon` on `IPlatformServices` (beside `FileSystem` and `Presence`), holding three leaf ports in `AgentGuard.Abstractions.Contracts`: `ISingleInstanceLock`, `IServiceManagerStart`, `ILoginRegistration`. A sub-container rather than three flat siblings because `AG0022` (`ContainerInterfaceSingleOwnerAnalyzer`, no test exemption) then covers the container and `AG0025` still covers each leaf through `BoundaryServices`' recursive walk — one extra type buys one extra rule's coverage. Each leaf is implemented internally per OS with a private ctor and a static `Create()`, reached only through the one `PlatformServices.Create()` door (`src/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.MacOS/Posix/PlatformServices.cs:21-48`). **This member/container shape is the public-interface change Tim reserved to himself — it needs his yes before ARCHITECTURE.**

**The load-bearing move: no string, path, or command crosses a daemon port.** `IServiceManagerStart.Start(ISystemServices, CancellationToken)` takes no binary path and no argv — the per-OS implementer composes `launchctl kickstart gui/<uid>/<label>`, `systemctl --user start agentguard-appd.service`, or `schtasks /Run /TN \AgentGuard\appd` from its own const owner. A caller therefore **cannot** express "launch this binary": risk (1) is not policed, it is impossible. `ISingleInstanceLock.Acquire`/`IsHeld` take no path either, so the daemon and a racing CLI probe cannot compute different lock paths — the two-daemon race dies at the type level. `ILoginRegistration.Register` is the one exception: it needs `~/.agentguard/bin/guard`, which `MachinePaths.BinGuardIn` (`src/AgentGuard.Engine/Setup/MachinePaths.cs:139`) owns in `AgentGuard.Engine`, an assembly the per-OS libraries cannot reference. It takes a `DaemonRegistration` DTO carrying only that path — mirroring `IPresenceCheck.Check(PresenceRequest, ISystemServices, CancellationToken)`, the proven shape.

**One gate owns the policy.** `DaemonGate` in `AgentGuard.Setup` — deliberately named after `ApprovalGate`, whose `AG0108` fence is the exact prior art — is the sole production caller of `IsHeld` and `Start`. `EnsureRunningAsync` probes the lock; if unheld it asks `ILoginRegistration.Detect`; a missing or wrong-binary registration fails closed with the cause and the fix (`guard install` / `guard doctor --fix`), never by registering itself, because registering is an approval-gated mutation and doing it here would route around `ApprovalGate`. `DaemonHost` (mirroring `GuardHost` for `hook`) is the sole caller of `Acquire`; it acquires first, throws and exits non-zero when it cannot, then idles on one cancellation-linked await. `LoginRegistrationCondition` is the sole caller of `Register`/`Detect` and lands in `SetupConditions.MachineStructural` + `Machine`, so `install` writes the registration and `doctor --fix` repairs it with no new `Program.cs` wiring.

**Zero P/Invoke.** Managed `FileStream`+`FileShare.None` on POSIX, managed `Local\` named `Mutex` on Windows, `Process` for all three service managers. Nothing here is native interop, so `AG0101`/`AG0113`'s closed hand-named presence-only exemption in `PresenceContracts.cs:227-229` never has to widen — the single most dangerous rule-change pressure in this issue, removed by Tim's `schtasks`-over-COM decision rather than by argument.

**AG0011 owner registration is narrow on purpose.** `Process`/`ProcessStartInfo` become legal only inside the three `IServiceManagerStart` implementers; `FileStream` and `Mutex` only inside the three `ISingleInstanceLock` implementers. Not a general `IProcessRunner` in `Boundaries` — that is the lazy registration, and it would hand every future agent a general shell-out. `System.Threading.Mutex` has no `OwnedPrimitives` entry today (grep: zero `Mutex` hits in `src`/`tests`), so it is currently legal everywhere; without the entry the Windows half of "exactly one runs at a time" has no build-time fence at all.

**POSIX source sharing.** The lock implementation is link-shared macOS→Linux like `PosixFileSystem`, with only the lock-directory resolution split into `private static partial` OS fragments — the same mechanism `PlatformServices.CreatePresence()` and `PosixFileSystem.TryQueryNativeCaseSensitivity` already use twice. `AG0037` already makes the lazy alternative (an `OperatingSystem.IsMacOS()` branch in the shared file) a build error. The macOS `AGS5443` suppression must sit on the macOS-only fragment, never on the link-shared file, or Tim's macOS-scoped exemption silently widens to Linux.

verdict.why:
Scored against the four rails, risk-first wins on three of them and loses only on DRY, where the fix is a clean graft.

rails-real-work (rails 1, 2, 8) is the decider. Risk-first is the only candidate that designs the type surface so the wrong daemon is inexpressible rather than merely policed. Its load-bearing move — no string, path, or command parameter crosses a daemon port, so `Start()` takes no argv and `TryAcquire()` takes no path — kills #63's central failure ("triggers that same canonical start rather than launching it some other way") at the type level, and kills the two-daemon race by making it impossible for a probe and a daemon to compute different lock paths. Simplest leaves `Register(string binaryPath)` open and then admits its own guard for it is "lower confidence — flagged for RULE-PHASE to assess feasibility"; most-general leaves the same hole. A convention you hope holds is exactly the shape rail 2 calls a hack.

rails-decisions produces the run-failing catch only risk-first made: the on-disk CONTENT of the LaunchAgent plist, the systemd unit, and the Task Scheduler task is best-practices 4b ("the on-disk layout of anything we write into the user's project or machine"), it is decided nowhere in the issue, conversation.md, or the tree, and so is a blocking `Violation — undecided forced choice`. Simplest and most-general both silently assume it is composable in code — a silent default on a 4b item. Risk-first also scoped the AGS5443 suppression to a macOS-only fragment after noticing that `AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Linux.csproj` link-shares the MacOS POSIX sources (verified live at lines 29-31), so a suppression on the shared file would silently widen Tim's macOS-only exemption to Linux. Neither other candidate saw that.

rails-solid-code: hanging the ports off `IPlatformServices` as a sub-container buys real existing coverage rather than new rules — verified that `BoundaryServices.ResolveTree` recurses through sub-container accessors, so AG0022 covers the container and AG0025 covers each leaf. Risk-first's rules are structural (parameter-shape, caller-table, value-scan) modeled on shipped mechanisms (AG0108, AG0111), not review conventions.

Where it loses: rails-dry-code rail 6. Registering `Process`/`ProcessStartInfo` to three per-OS start implementers writes the same start/wait/exit-code block three times across three projects — the copies-across-modules case the rail names explicitly, invisible to the in-build analyzers. Most-general and simplest both got this right, and most-general got the placement argument exactly right against best-practices 2d with live evidence (`CrossPlatformAdapters.cs` doc: "owners-live-at-lowest-consumer"; `RandomGeneratorAdapter` in core `AgentGuard.CrossPlatform`; verified `InternalsVisibleTo` grants to all three per-OS assemblies). Risk-first's stated objection was to "a general `IProcessRunner` in Boundaries" — a placement no candidate actually proposed — so the graft answers its real concern rather than overriding it.
verdict.synthesizedApproach:
DECIDE FIRST — three items block ARCHITECTURE, none may be defaulted:
(1) The member shape: `IPlatformServices.Daemon` returning a sub-container `IPlatformDaemon` holding three leaves (`ISingleInstanceLock`, `IServiceManagerStart`, `ILoginRegistration`). Tim reserved this ("tried to lock in a desgin too early (we don't know how many properties and classes we need yet)"). Recommended over three flat siblings because the extra type buys AG0022 container coverage on top of AG0025 leaf coverage — verified that `BoundaryServices.ResolveTree` recurses into sub-container accessors.
(2) The on-disk content of the plist, the systemd unit, and the Task Scheduler task definition — best-practices 4b, decided nowhere. Also whether that content is composed in code or shipped as a template under `eng/` beside `agentguard-presence.policy`.
(3) One new member on `IPlatformFileSystem`, `EnsurePrivateDirectory(string path)` — a public-interface change, small but not foldable into (1).

THE SHAPE. One sub-container `IPlatformDaemon` on `IPlatformServices` (beside the existing `FileSystem` and `Presence` — verified those are the only two members today), holding three leaf ports in `AgentGuard.Abstractions.Contracts`, each implemented internally per OS with a private constructor and a static `Create()`, reached only through the one `PlatformServices.Create()` door.

THE LOAD-BEARING MOVE — no string, path, or command crosses a daemon port. `IServiceManagerStart.Start(ISystemServices, CancellationToken)` takes no binary path and no argv; the per-OS implementer composes `launchctl kickstart gui/<uid>/<label>`, `systemctl --user start agentguard-appd.service`, or `schtasks /Run /TN \AgentGuard\appd` from its own const. A caller cannot express "launch this binary", so the divergent second start path is not policed — it is unexpressible. `ISingleInstanceLock.Acquire`/`IsHeld` take no path either, so a racing CLI probe and a starting daemon cannot compute different lock paths. `ILoginRegistration.Register`/`Detect` is the one exception: it needs `~/.agentguard/bin/guard`, owned by `MachinePaths.BinGuardIn` in `AgentGuard.Engine` — an assembly the per-OS libraries cannot reference — so it takes a `DaemonRegistration` DTO carrying only that path.

THE PARAMETER SHAPE IS FORCED, NOT CHOSEN (graft, most-general; corrected by the judge). `PlatformServices.Create()` is parameter-less and must stay so: handing it a Boundaries-built service is the inverted dependency SOLID rail 8 and best-practices 2d forbid, since `SystemServices.Create()` builds `platform` before it builds `environment`. Per-OS ports therefore reach owned services at call time through `ISystemServices`, exactly as `IPresenceCheck.Check(PresenceRequest, ISystemServices, CancellationToken)` does. This is not a preference: AG0031 (`NoServiceAsParameterAnalyzer`, verified) bans a leaf boundary service interface as a method parameter, so most-general's own keyStep of passing `IFileReader`/`IFileWriter` explicitly is a build error, while the container itself is not a leaf and stays legal.

ONE SHARED PROCESS-LAUNCH OWNER (graft, most-general + simplest — the correction to risk-first). `IProcessLauncher`, a faithful `Process.Start`/`WaitForExitAsync`/`ExitCode` mirror (best-practices 2c), with one OS-uniform implementer `ProcessLauncherAdapter`, both INTERNAL to core `AgentGuard.CrossPlatform` — not in `Abstractions.Contracts`, where both runners-up wrongly placed it: a Contracts interface is public and would hand Engine and the CLI a general shell-out, and most-general's own auto-resolved record says it must never be exposed on a container. Core CrossPlatform is the lowest actual consumer (verified: it already grants `InternalsVisibleTo` to all three per-OS assemblies, and each per-OS `PlatformServices.Create()` already calls `PlatformFileSystemComposition.Create()` directly), so the dependency points one way and `Process`/`ProcessStartInfo` need exactly ONE owner entry instead of three. Risk-first's fear of "a general shell-out for every future agent" is answered structurally, not by duplication: the launcher is internal, its callers are an explicit allowlist, and the tool-name value ban keeps every command line inside the one per-OS start owner.

THE LOCK IS ONE OWNER SERVING TWO LEDGER ROWS (graft, simplest). `single-instance-lock` and `lock-liveness-probe` both ruled "new", but Tim's recorded decision treats them as one object used two ways — "there is nothing extra to build and nothing that can disagree with it". `DaemonHost` calls `Acquire` and holds the handle for the process lifetime; `DaemonGate` calls `IsHeld`. `daemon-process-lifetime` needs no third mechanism at all. Managed `FileStream` + `FileShare.None` on POSIX, managed `Local\` named `Mutex` on Windows, `schtasks` rather than Task Scheduler COM on Windows — so this design is zero P/Invoke and the closed, hand-named presence-only native-interop exemption in `PresenceContracts.cs` never has to widen.

THE 0700 DIRECTORY REUSES AN EXISTING OWNER (graft, simplest). The POSIX lock needs `agentguard/` at mode 0700 before it opens the lock file; raw `Directory.CreateDirectory` + `SetUnixFileMode` there is already AG0101's (verified: it owns exactly those OS-divergent statics). Rather than a fourth interface, grow one member on the interface that already owns this concern — `IPlatformFileSystem.EnsurePrivateDirectory(string path)` (POSIX bodies real, Windows throws, mirroring the existing MakeExecutable precedent). It then inherits AG0025/AG0030/AG0101 protection with no analyzer change. Surface it to Tim as its own public-interface change.

POSIX SOURCE SHARING AND THE SUPPRESSION. The lock implementation is link-shared macOS to Linux like `PosixFileSystem` (verified in `AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Linux.csproj:29-31`), with only the lock-directory resolution split into `private static partial` OS fragments — the same mechanism `PlatformServices.CreatePresence()` already uses. The `AGS5443` suppression sits on the macOS-only fragment, never on the link-shared file, or Tim's macOS-scoped exemption silently widens to Linux where `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is not the temp root.

ENGINE AND CLI. `DaemonGate` in `AgentGuard.Setup`, named after `ApprovalGate` whose AG0108 fence is the prior art, is the sole production caller of `IsHeld` and `Start`: `EnsureRunningAsync` probes the lock, and when unheld asks `ILoginRegistration.Detect` and fails closed with the cause and the fix (`guard install`, `guard doctor --fix`) rather than registering itself — registering is an ApprovalGate-gated mutation and doing it here routes around the gate. `DaemonHost` is the sole caller of `Acquire`: acquire first, exit non-zero with an actionable message when it cannot, then one cancellation-linked await through `services.Clock`. `LoginRegistrationCondition : ISetupCondition` is the sole caller of `Register`/`Detect` and lands in `SetupConditions.MachineStructural` (after `BinSymlinkCondition`, so it points at the launcher that condition establishes) and `SetupConditions.Machine`, so `install` writes it and `doctor --fix` repairs it with zero new `Program.cs` wiring (verified: `SetupCommands` iterates the lists at lines 149-187).

THE INSTALL CALL SITE (graft, most-general). `SetupCommands.Install` calls `DaemonGate.EnsureRunningAsync` once after its condition loop succeeds. This is the one call site #63's own Done-when line requires — "the CLI starts it through the same canonical path when it is not running" — and it covers the case the issue names, installing onto an already-running login session. Simplest correctly flagged that without this the design ships no CLI-visible proof of that acceptance line.

`status` IS ALREADY DECIDED — DO NOT RE-OPEN IT. Simplest surfaced "does `status` trigger the start?" as an open fork. conversation.md answers it in Tim's recorded words: "`status` stays narrower: it answers whether appd is running now. The registration is install wiring and belongs to `install` and `doctor`." Bringing a settled answer as a decision is itself a rails-decisions violation. `status` is a read-only probe over `DaemonGate`; `install` and any future consumer own the check-and-start.

BLOCKING UNDECIDED FORCED CHOICE — the on-disk content of the LaunchAgent plist, the systemd user unit, and the Task Scheduler task definition is 'the on-disk layout of anything we write into the user's project or machine' (best-practices 4b, reserved for Tim) and is decided nowhere in the live issue, conversation.md, or the tree. So is whether that content is composed in code or shipped as a template file under `eng/` like `agentguard-presence.policy`. No contract advances to IMPLEMENT with these open. Only risk-first caught this; the other two candidates silently assumed code composition.

The register-then-start round trip was never spiked. Writing the plist or unit file may not be sufficient by itself for an immediate `launchctl kickstart` / `systemctl --user start` to succeed in the same already-running login session — launchd may need `launchctl bootstrap` and systemd may need `systemctl --user daemon-reload` and/or `enable` before the new registration is findable, and a written-but-unenabled unit silently fails 'appd starts at login' on Linux specifically. The recorded spike proved lock semantics only. This does not change the interface shape proposed here, but it changes what each per-OS `Register()` body must do and should be nailed down empirically before IMPLEMENT, not assumed.

The Windows Task Scheduler creation flags (`/SC ONLOGON` vs `ONSTART`, `/RL HIGHEST`, `/IT` for desktop/interactive-token access) are unsettled anywhere in the issue, conversation.md, or the tree, and bear directly on #63's Done-when line 'the process type chosen can draw a window when part 3 needs it to'. No Windows spike exists the way a macOS one does.

`System.Threading.Mutex` has no `OwnedPrimitives` entry today — verified by grep, zero occurrences in `src`, `tests`, `analyzers`, or `eng`. conversation.md leaves the question to RULE-PHASE. If RULE-PHASE does not add the entry, the Windows half of 'exactly one runs at a time' ships with no build-time fence at all and any class can mint a second named mutex.

AGS5443 fires at every `GetTempDirectory()` call site unconditionally and Tim's exemption is macOS-only. The POSIX lock source is link-shared macOS to Linux by the existing csproj `<Compile Include ... Link>` mechanism (verified at `AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Linux.csproj:29-31`), so a suppression placed on the shared file compiles into the Linux assembly and silently widens the approved exemption to an OS where `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is not the temp root. The lock-directory resolution must be an OS-suffixed `private static partial` fragment, macOS only.

`ILoginRegistration.Register` needs `~/.agentguard/bin/guard`, whose single owner `MachinePaths.BinGuardIn` lives in `AgentGuard.Engine` — an assembly the per-OS libraries cannot reference. Recomputing the path inside a per-OS assembly creates a second path owner (DRY rail 5); adding the project reference would invert the dependency (best-practices 2d, Tim's personal sign-off required anywhere in any repo). The DTO hand-off is the only route that violates neither.

AG0031 (`NoServiceAsParameterAnalyzer`, verified) bans a leaf boundary service interface as a method parameter, and the derived service set includes `IFileReader`/`IFileWriter`. Any design that hands owned boundary services to a per-OS daemon port as explicit method arguments is a build error — most-general's own keyStep proposed exactly that. The only compliant shape is the `IPresenceCheck.Check(request, ISystemServices, ct)` container-at-call-time shape, which is also forced by `PlatformServices.Create()` having to stay parameter-less.

Neither AG0025 nor AG0114 protects the internal `IProcessLauncher` owner. Verified: AG0025's candidate set is derived entirely from the `ISystemServices` container walk and the launcher is deliberately not on the container; AG0114 is a closed, hand-named presence-scoped list. This gap needs the explicit RULE-PHASE fix listed above, not an assumed one.

Coverage exposure: three per-OS lock implementers, three registration implementers, and one shared launcher, each exercised on one CI leg under a per-assembly 75% floor, so a Windows implementer at 0% can hide under the assembly total. The Linux leg runs `ubuntu-24.04-arm` (ARM64) only, and conversation.md states plainly: 'Nothing above was run on Linux or Windows.' Additionally, `RequiresNativeSpecTestAttribute` is `AttributeTargets.Interface` and the convention test scans the per-OS production assembly, while the daemon ports are declared in `AgentGuard.Abstractions.Contracts` — the marker wiring must be settled, not assumed.

If IMPLEMENT reaches for the Windows Task Scheduler COM API instead of `schtasks`, it lands on AG0008/AG0101/AG0113, whose native-interop exemption is a closed hand-named presence-only list in `PresenceContracts.cs` with no generic path — and the natural next move is a suppression, which is a top-severity Lie-catcher finding. Tim's recorded `schtasks` decision is what keeps this design at zero P/Invoke and must be carried into the contract's Decisions section verbatim, or an implementer will re-derive it wrongly.

GROUND's `per-os-port-pattern` autoResolved record justifies the raw-`Process` ban by citing 'the project's own already-recorded AG0013 ruling'. AG0013 is retired — folded into AG0011 before any release and listed as retired in `AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md` (verified). The contract must cite AG0011; a stale id in a Decisions record is what the Lie-catcher rules against. conversation.md already flags this correction.

`DaemonGate.EnsureRunningAsync` must never repair a missing or wrong login registration, only diagnose it and name the fix. Writing the registration is an ApprovalGate-gated mutation owned by `install`; doing it from an ungated command would route a gated mutation around the gate. The one-caller-per-port-member rule covers this only if its table lists `LoginRegistrationCondition` as the sole caller of `Register`.

This design adds a meaningful surface — one sub-container, three ports, one internal launcher plus its handle type, roughly eight concrete classes, one new `IPlatformFileSystem` member, and two CLI verbs — for an issue framed as 'just a process that starts, stays up, and can be found'. That size is the deliberate cost of building the full general seam once (SOLID rail 7) rather than a per-call hack, and is stated plainly rather than hidden.

The AGS5443 suppression and all three `OwnedPrimitives.cs` entries (Process/ProcessStartInfo, FileStream, and the new Mutex row) must be carried into the contract's Decisions section verbatim. conversation.md names the first two as items that 'fail the run outright if they are missing', not as minor documentation gaps.

The general version of the suppression-allowlist rule — an allowlist for suppressing any `AG*`/`AGS*` diagnostic, the 'fix the class, not the instance' shape — is out of this issue's scope. File it as a GitHub issue the moment the contract is written rather than recording it as a note.

autoResolved.resolution: An interface in `AgentGuard.Abstractions.Contracts`, implemented internally per OS in `AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.{MacOS,Linux,Windows}` with a private constructor and a static `Create()`, hung off `IPlatformServices` and reached only through the one `PlatformServices.Create()` door. Never a direct OS call from the Engine or the CLI.
autoResolved.principle: Best-practices guide 2a (nothing reaches the outside world except through an interface we own) and 1b (OS-agnostic by default; OS-difference is the rare exception, isolated behind the platform interface).
autoResolved.evidence: Verified live: `src/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.MacOS/Posix/PlatformServices.cs` has a private constructor and a parameterless `public static IPlatformServices Create()` taking no passed-in service; `src/AgentGuard.Abstractions/Contracts/IPlatformServices.cs` exposes exactly `FileSystem` and `Presence` today and documents itself as 'designed to grow'; `PlatformServices.Linux.cs` supplies `CreatePresence() => LinuxPresenceCheck.Create(new TmdsPolkitAuthority())`. conversation.md records Tim concurring with this structure: 'it got the most important thing right which was the assembly and cross plat structure'.

autoResolved.choice: Whether the daemon may call launchctl/systemctl/schtasks, `FileStream`, or `Mutex` directly, or must grow owners for them.
